subject: Geography
central_question: How do India’s location, extent, size and relations with neighbouring regions shape its physical diversity and geographical importance?
in_scope_units: India’s latitudinal and longitudinal extent and their implications.
Indian Standard Time and the purpose of the standard meridian.
India’s size, coastline, islands and physical diversity.
The Indian subcontinent and the role of surrounding mountains and seas.
India’s position in Asia and its land and maritime neighbours.
Map-based exercises on location, boundaries and administrative divisions.
banned_topics: Detailed physiographic divisions, which belong to Structure and Physiography.
The mechanism and seasons of the monsoon, which belong to Climate.
Detailed river systems, which belong to Drainage System.

known_pitfalls.claim: India uses the local solar time of every city as official time.
known_pitfalls.correction: India follows one Indian Standard Time based on 82°30′ E longitude.

known_pitfalls.claim: Equal angular north–south and east–west spans give equal ground distances.
known_pitfalls.correction: The north–south distance is 3,214 km and the east–west distance is 2,933 km because meridians converge poleward.

known_pitfalls.claim: India’s territorial limit ends at the coastline.
known_pitfalls.correction: It extends 12 nautical miles, about 21.9 km, from the coast.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sri Lanka shares a land boundary with India.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is separated from India by the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Strait.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Indian subcontinent consists only of India.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter includes Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and India.

recommended_example_progression: Use Figure 1.1 to identify India’s extreme latitudes and longitudes.
Use Exercise 1(iv) to recognise 82°30′ E as India’s standard meridian.
Use Exercise 2(iv) to explain why watches in Kohima and New Delhi show the same time.
Use Project/Activity items (iii)–(v) to identify coastal states, land-boundary states and coastal Union Territories.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter section contains Exercises 1(i–iv), 2(i–iv), and a seven-part Project/Activity based on maps, an atlas and census data.
